section_summary: This section chiefly documents U.S. State, Commerce, and Army processing of applications by foreign and American commercial travelers seeking entry into occupied Japan, Korea, and Okinawa. It covers military permits, theater clearances, exit-permit waivers, rejected applications, diplomatic requests, and instructions transmitted to consulates and occupation authorities. Significant cases include Michiel Onnes, Ethelred O. Taunton, D. C. Matthai, Hira Singh, David Green, George Terk, Sanga Nilkamhaeng, Moise Moiseeff, and Nissim S. Tawil, as well as Brazilian proposals concerning Japanese passengers and repatriates.

subfiles.title: Letter concerning a permit for Solomon Dabah
subfiles.from: Walter F. Chappell, Department of State
subfiles.about: Directs Solomon Dabah to apply through the Commerce Department for permission to enter Japan.
subfiles.summary: State explains that Commerce, not State, submits private traders' applications to the military authorities.

subfiles.title: Transmission of military permit no. 340
subfiles.from: Walter F. Chappell, Department of State
subfiles.about: Transmits Solomon Dabah's June entry permit and requests his departure details.
subfiles.summary: Dabah must report his itinerary for an exit waiver or reapply if the permit's validity is unsuitable.

subfiles.title: Army policy on changing permit dates
subfiles.about: Records a discussion with Captain Rawls about military-permit validity dates.
subfiles.summary: The Army will no longer alter permit dates; dissatisfied travelers must reapply through regular channels.

subfiles.title: Clearance telegram for Robert Liewer
subfiles.about: Notifies the consul that Robert Liewer may enter Japan during May for business.
subfiles.summary: Liewer may stay sixty days and must carry photographs and a certified copy of the telegram.

subfiles.title: File memorandum on Robert Liewer's postponed travel
subfiles.about: Explains Liewer's new May clearance and changed location from Saigon to Hong Kong.
subfiles.summary: Miss Curran requested that the paid clearance telegram be redirected to Liewer at the Repulse Bay Hotel.

subfiles.title: Army list of commercial clearances
subfiles.from: J. D. Scott, Military Permit Section
subfiles.about: Reports May entry clearances for Chon Nien Hsieh and Robert Liewer.
subfiles.summary: Both travelers received sixty-day commercial clearances and were required to carry two passport photographs.

subfiles.title: Korean clearance for Michiel Onnes
subfiles.from: J. D. Scott, Military Permit Section
subfiles.about: Reports approval for Michiel Onnes to enter Korea from Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Onnes may enter Korea between May 3 and June 3 for thirty days with samples and personal effects.

subfiles.title: Commercial data sheet for Michiel Onnes
subfiles.about: Supplies business information for Onnes's proposed Korean travel.
subfiles.summary: Lists Van Reekum Paper, Onnes's position, paper products, capitalization, and prewar Korean trade.

subfiles.title: Application by Michiel Onnes
subfiles.about: Requests permission to visit Korea on behalf of Van Reekum Paper.
subfiles.summary: Describes the firm's paper products, history, capitalization, and approximately $75,000 in prewar Korean business.

subfiles.title: Telephone notification of Onnes's clearance
subfiles.about: Records notice to Van Reekum Paper that Onnes may enter Korea.
subfiles.summary: The company promised to cable Onnes and direct him to the U.S. Political Adviser's Office.

subfiles.title: Telegram authorizing Onnes's Korean entry
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Requests assistance documenting Michiel Onnes's approved entry into Korea.
subfiles.summary: Onnes was authorized to enter Korea for thirty days, carry commercial samples, and report to the Visitors Information Center. Van Reekum Paper was charged for the message.

subfiles.title: Clearance for Walter M. Schapiro
subfiles.from: J. D. Scott, Military Permit Section
subfiles.about: Reports that Walter M. Schapiro may travel from Bombay to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Schapiro was cleared to enter between May 5 and June 5 for a thirty-day stay.

subfiles.title: Rejection of Giacomo Mensace for Okinawa
subfiles.from: J. D. Scott, Military Permit Section
subfiles.about: Reports that Giacomo Mensace cannot enter Okinawa because he is Italian.
subfiles.summary: Military authorities had conditioned clearance on American citizenship and therefore rejected Mensace.

subfiles.title: Telegram to Shanghai referencing telegram 809
subfiles.about: Sends a reply concerning the consul's telegram 809 of April 9.
subfiles.summary: The surviving copy contains addressing and routing information, but no substantive message text.

subfiles.title: Brasiltur inquiry concerning Japanese passengers
subfiles.from: U.S. Embassy, Rio de Janeiro, forwarding Companhia Brasileira de Turismo
subfiles.to: Secretary of State, for SCAP Tokyo
subfiles.about: Asks whether Japanese passengers may visit Japan and return to Brazil aboard the same ship.
subfiles.summary: Brasiltur also asks whether Brazilian-born persons of Japanese parentage may leave Japan for Brazil with proper documentation.

subfiles.title: Clearance for Lieutenant Udom Sangkasaba
subfiles.from: J. D. Scott, Military Permit Section
subfiles.about: Reports no military objection to Sangkasaba's entry into Japan.
subfiles.summary: Sangkasaba may enter June 15–July 15 for sixty days and must carry two photographs.

subfiles.title: Notification to Siam of Sangkasaba's clearance
subfiles.about: Confirms permission for Lieutenant Sangkasaba to enter Japan.
subfiles.summary: The note specifies his entry window, sixty-day stay, photograph requirement, and passport endorsement under SCAP Circular 8.

subfiles.title: Request to Army for Sangkasaba clearance
subfiles.about: Forwards Siam's request for Sangkasaba to purchase fishing equipment in Japan.
subfiles.summary: State asks the Army to obtain SCAP's decision; a theater-clearance memorandum would suffice if approved.

subfiles.title: Taunton telegram requesting his permit
subfiles.about: Requests confirmation that his Japan permit has been mailed.
subfiles.summary: Taunton asks for a collect reply confirming immediate dispatch of the permit.

subfiles.title: Telephone arrangements for Taunton's permit
subfiles.about: Records arrangements with Mr. Hoffmeister to send Taunton's permit to Houston.
subfiles.summary: Corkran requested Taunton's departure details so State could arrange an exit-permit waiver.

subfiles.title: Taunton application to visit Japan
subfiles.from: Ethelred O. Taunton and Hugo A. Dixon
subfiles.to: Departments of Commerce and State and SCAP
subfiles.about: Requests permanent commercial residence in Japan for McFadden's raw-cotton agent.
subfiles.summary: The application describes extensive prewar cotton sales and planned visits to Kobe, Osaka, Tokyo, and Yokohama.

subfiles.title: Taunton's supporting letter to Commerce
subfiles.to: Department of Commerce Regional Office, Memphis
subfiles.about: Supplies passport, vaccination, and sailing information supporting Taunton's Japan application.
subfiles.summary: Taunton planned to sail from New Orleans aboard the Tillie Lykes on May 16.

subfiles.title: Commerce endorsement of Taunton's application
subfiles.about: Forwards and strongly recommends Taunton's application.
subfiles.summary: Fontaine describes McFadden as a large, reputable cotton firm and endorses Hugo Dixon's representations.

subfiles.title: Exit-permit waiver for Taunton
subfiles.about: Waives Taunton's exit permit for departure from New Orleans.
subfiles.summary: The waiver covers his May 16 sailing to Japan aboard the Tillie Lykes.

subfiles.title: Taunton's departure-details telegram
subfiles.about: Reports the ports and dates of Taunton's planned departure.
subfiles.summary: Taunton expected the Tillie Lykes to leave Galveston before its final May 16 departure from New Orleans.

subfiles.title: Reply concerning Taunton's permit and exit clearance
subfiles.about: Confirms dispatch of Taunton's permit and arrangements for departure without an exit document.
subfiles.summary: State mailed the permit to Houston and would notify New Orleans immigration officers of the waiver.

subfiles.title: Transmission of Taunton military permit no. 330
subfiles.about: Encloses Taunton's Army permit to enter Japan.
subfiles.summary: State again requests his departure place and date so the exit-permit requirement can be waived.

subfiles.title: Speedletter concerning D. C. Matthai
subfiles.about: Asks Pan-American to direct Matthai to his military permit at American Express.
subfiles.summary: The permit and exit-clearance instructions awaited Matthai at American Express in San Francisco.

subfiles.title: Indian Embassy call concerning Matthai's mail
subfiles.about: Records Mr. Banerji's concern that Matthai might not collect his permit from American Express.
subfiles.summary: Banerji requested a warning through Pan-American, where Matthai had to arrange onward travel to Japan.

subfiles.title: Action slip forwarding Matthai's permit
subfiles.about: Forwards Duleep Cherian Matthai's Japan military permit.
subfiles.summary: The Army asks State to mail the enclosed permit to Matthai at American Express in San Francisco.

subfiles.title: Transmission of Matthai military permit no. 331
subfiles.about: Encloses a permit valid for one journey to Japan between May 15 and June 15.
subfiles.summary: Matthai must report his departure details and transportation so State can arrange an exit waiver.

subfiles.title: Application for Nefen J. Sbath to visit Japan
subfiles.from: Nefen J. Sbath and Paul E. Sernau
subfiles.about: Requests commercial entry to Japan for a Syrian representative.
subfiles.summary: The applicant intended to visit Tokyo, Osaka, and Nagoya for two weeks to buy merchandise and investigate supply opportunities.

subfiles.title: Reaffirmation of Hira Singh's exit clearance
subfiles.about: Records action after Hira Singh postponed his departure to May 14.
subfiles.summary: Immigration officials were asked to reaffirm Singh's previously arranged San Francisco exit permission.

subfiles.title: Revised departure notice for Hira Singh
subfiles.about: Reports Hira Singh's revised departure date for Japan.
subfiles.summary: Singh would leave San Francisco by Pan American Airways on May 14 using military permit 12444.

subfiles.title: Exit-permit waiver for Hira Singh
subfiles.about: Waives Hira Singh's exit permit for air departure from San Francisco.
subfiles.summary: The waiver initially covered Singh's planned May 7 departure under military permit 12444.

subfiles.title: Hira Singh application to visit Japan
subfiles.from: Hira Singh and Barret Textile Corporation
subfiles.to: Departments of Commerce and State and SCAP
subfiles.about: Requests permission for Singh to establish textile-trade relations in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Singh planned to visit Osaka, Kobe, Nagoya, and Kyoto to purchase and trade finished textiles through the Japanese Board of Trade.

subfiles.title: Army clearance for George Terk and David Green
subfiles.about: Reports commercial clearances for George Terk and David Green, then in Hong Kong.
subfiles.summary: Both could enter Japan by June 15 for sixty days and were required to carry passport photographs.

subfiles.title: Application for David Green to visit Japan
subfiles.from: Werner R. Voigt, Wyeth International Limited
subfiles.about: Requests entry for David Green to investigate Japanese markets for Wyeth products.
subfiles.summary: Green, a British partner based in Hong Kong, planned a three-month visit to Tokyo to assess future business possibilities.

subfiles.title: Telephone notification of David Green's clearance
subfiles.about: Records notification to Werner R. Voigt that David Green had been cleared.
subfiles.summary: Voigt asked State to notify Hong Kong and promised to cable Green directly.

subfiles.title: Clearance telegram for David Green
subfiles.about: Notifies the consul of Green's permission to enter Japan for business.
subfiles.summary: Green could enter before June 15 for sixty days and receive a certified copy as documentation.

subfiles.title: Reply to Rio concerning Brasiltur plans
subfiles.about: Rejects Brasiltur's proposed tourist voyage and explains Japanese entry and departure rules.
subfiles.summary: Japanese nationals could return only as permanent repatriates, while temporary visitors required individual permits. Brazilian nationals of Japanese origin could leave Japan with appropriate passports and SCAP exit permits.

subfiles.title: Largely illegible incoming telegram
subfiles.about: An incoming telegram associated with the Japan travel file.
subfiles.summary: Only routing marks, filing data, and isolated words remain legible in the OCR.

subfiles.title: Tradelines letter requesting a replacement permit
subfiles.from: Lionel L. Blattner, Tradelines International Corporation
subfiles.about: Requests a later military permit for Nessim Frangi.
subfiles.summary: The page retains chiefly the firm's letterhead; the request is identified by State's reply.

subfiles.title: Reply on Nessim Frangi's permit
subfiles.about: Directs Tradelines to reapply through Commerce for an October permit.
subfiles.summary: State explains it cannot issue permits and asks for return of Frangi's unused permit.

subfiles.title: Alice Florea's departure notice
subfiles.about: Reports Florea's planned June 12 sailing from San Francisco.
subfiles.summary: Florea acknowledges military permit 230 and asks where her exit permit will be available.

subfiles.title: Exit-permit waiver for Alice Florea
subfiles.about: Waives Alice Florea's exit permit for her June 12 sailing.
subfiles.summary: The waiver covers departure from San Francisco aboard the General Meigs.

subfiles.title: Notification of Florea's exit waiver
subfiles.about: Confirms arrangements for Florea to leave without an exit-permit document.
subfiles.summary: Immigration officers at San Francisco would be notified of her clearance.

subfiles.title: Action slip on Alfred Bridi
subfiles.from: J. D. Scott, Military Permit Section
subfiles.about: Records telephone clearance for Alfred Bridi to enter Japan.
subfiles.summary: Bridi could enter during July for sixty days and later seek semi-permanent residence from occupation authorities.

subfiles.title: Notification of George Terk's clearance
subfiles.about: Records notification to Alexander Terk of his son's theater clearance.
subfiles.summary: Alexander Terk asked State to notify Hong Kong at his company's expense.

subfiles.title: Army memorandum on Terk and Green
subfiles.about: Reports Japan clearances for George Terk and David Green in Hong Kong.
subfiles.summary: They could enter May 15–June 15 for sixty days and must carry two passport photographs.

subfiles.title: Exit-permit waiver for George Terk
subfiles.about: Waives George Terk's exit permit for his April 1 flight.
subfiles.summary: Terk would leave Minneapolis for Japan under the traders' quota.

subfiles.title: Clearance telegram for George Terk
subfiles.about: Notifies the consul of Terk's permission to enter Japan for business.
subfiles.summary: Terk could enter before June 15 for sixty days and receive a certified copy as documentation.

subfiles.title: Army advice on Paul Chryssanthopoulos Jr.
subfiles.about: Advises that the Greek applicant's case should proceed through Sweden.
subfiles.summary: The Army declines the vague application because Sweden acts as Greece's protecting power in Japan.

subfiles.title: Note to Greece on protective-power procedure
subfiles.about: Explains how Greek nationals should apply for travel to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Because Sweden protects Greek interests in Japan, Chryssanthopoulos's application and future Greek applications should reach SCAP through Swedish diplomatic channels.

subfiles.title: British Embassy request for six Okinawa visitors
subfiles.about: Requests permission for six British subjects to inspect purchased property on Okinawa.
subfiles.summary: The group would inspect ships, materials, and scrap acquired through U.S. liquidation and maritime agencies.

subfiles.title: Discussions concerning the six Okinawa applicants
subfiles.about: Records Jesse Briegel's efforts to secure Okinawa entry for six British subjects.
subfiles.summary: Captain Rawls said Okinawa's commander controlled entry but would cable applications requested by State. Corkran required formal British Embassy sponsorship, which Briegel supplied, and Briegel claimed MacArthur's staff would overturn any refusal.

subfiles.title: Submission of six Okinawa applications to the Army
subfiles.about: Requests Okinawa permission for six British nationals inspecting purchased ships and scrap.
subfiles.summary: State requests theater clearance for four applicants in Hong Kong and military permits for two in New York.

subfiles.title: Argentine note concerning Américo Guerra
subfiles.about: Explains the commercial purpose of Américo Guerra's proposed Japan trip.
subfiles.summary: Guerra sought to resume longstanding dealings with Iida and Company and represented an Argentine commercial firm.

subfiles.title: Inquiry into Siamese counselor's Japan stop
subfiles.about: Records additional information requested for Sanga Nilkamhaeng's visit.
subfiles.summary: Nilkamhaeng expected to arrive June 6 or 7, stay about two days, and visit friends in Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Siamese request for Nilkamhaeng party visas
subfiles.about: Requests visas allowing Counselor Nilkamhaeng and his party to pass through Japan.
subfiles.summary: The five-person party would fly June 4 to China via Japan after Nilkamhaeng's transfer to Nanking.

subfiles.title: Request to Army for Nilkamhaeng transit clearance
subfiles.about: Forwards Siam's request for Nilkamhaeng to stop briefly in Japan.
subfiles.summary: State asks the Army to obtain SCAP's decision on the party's proposed one- or two-day Tokyo visit.

subfiles.title: Envelope from Moise Moiseeff
subfiles.about: Air-mail envelope for Moiseeff's letter concerning Japan travel.
subfiles.summary: The envelope gives Moiseeff's care-of address at A. Ponve Company in San Francisco.

subfiles.title: Moiseeff's departure and reentry inquiry
subfiles.about: Reports Moiseeff's sailing date and asks about exit clearance needed for a reentry permit.
subfiles.summary: Moiseeff planned to sail from San Francisco June 12 aboard the General Meigs, arriving at Yokohama June 26.

subfiles.title: Reply confirming Moiseeff's exit waiver
subfiles.about: Confirms that Moiseeff may depart without an exit-permit document.
subfiles.summary: State suggests presenting the letter to San Francisco immigration officers when applying for his reentry permit.

subfiles.title: Exit-permit waiver for Moise Moiseeff
subfiles.about: Waives Moiseeff's exit permit for his June 12 sailing.
subfiles.summary: The Belgian applicant would leave San Francisco for Japan under the traders' quota.

subfiles.title: Confidential rejection of Nissim S. Tawil
subfiles.about: Reports that military authorities rejected Tawil's application for Japan.
subfiles.summary: A confidential cable alleged that Tawil was unscrupulous and had engaged in black-market operations before leaving Japan in 1946.

subfiles.title: Application for Nissim S. Tawil to visit Japan
subfiles.from: Harry S. Tawil and Nissim S. Tawil
subfiles.about: Requests commercial entry for Nissim Tawil to establish a Tokyo branch and buy Japanese goods.
subfiles.summary: The application identifies Tawil as a British Palestinian agent and lists textiles and sundries, prewar Kobe representation, intended cities, and a six-month stay.

subfiles.title: Notice of Tawil's application refusal
subfiles.about: Notifies Tawil that the Army refused his application to enter Japan.
subfiles.summary: The brief letter gives no reason for the refusal.

subfiles.title: Commerce list of approved Japan applicants
subfiles.from: Michael Lee, Office of International Trade
subfiles.about: Forwards applicants approved by Commerce for travel to Japan and Korea, subject to SCAP approval.
subfiles.summary: The attached list names Arnold Hartmann, Charles E. Tuttle, Joichi Nishihara, Henry T. Omano, and Howard T. Pung. It records citizenship, desired entry dates, transportation, and Pung's earlier Japan permit and passport numbers.
